judge.counterfactual: Had the applicant in [T001] §4 withheld the workloadMix and internal schedule confidence (as the note itself anticipates the production regime would require), the utility's Class B reasoning in [T002] would have been unchanged while privacy_integrity rose to 5 and applicant_experience to 5 — demonstrating that the disclosure was decision-irrelevant.

rationales.stakeholder_alignment: All three parties operate on a consistent fact base throughout. The applicant in [T001] discloses the full reference plan including the 180 MW capacity, Q4 2028 COD, 22% flexibility, and 55/45 workload mix. The utility in [T002] accurately recapitulates these values (e.g., parcel OWL-180MW-P1, 180 MW single-phase, Q3 2028–Q1 2029 requested band) before correcting the band to Q4 2028–Q2 2029 with an explicit timing rationale — this is a substantive disagreement on the band but not a misalignment on facts or policy. The regulator in [T003] cleanly reconstructs each party's position and the policy anchors (Order 2023 §§219–222, PJM Manual 14A §4.4, Manual 19 §5.3). No turn exposes a prior misunderstanding of what was disclosed; the band divergence is a negotiation, not a misalignment.
rationales.planning_defensibility: The utility planning lead in [T002] routes to First-Ready Fast Tier (conditional on deposit) and commits to an energization band without any clarification round. The filing in [T001] supplies parcel ID, single-phase 180 MW, COD, quantified flexibility (22%), redundancy shift (18%), applicant schedule confidence (~0.68), backup generation and BESS specs — i.e., load-profile confidence band, ResponseClass-equivalent flexibility, firmness rationale, and site-control class are all present at cluster-study precision. However, [T002] does not cite the policy version by hash (only generic 'Order 2023' reference), and the readiness-deposit tier is noted as 'non-negotiable' but no specific $/MW tier (e.g., PJM Cycle 1 $4,000/MW) is identified; the flexibility class parameters [X%, N events, H hours] are explicitly deferred to the interconnection agreement rather than set in the decision. These are one-step-short-of-perfect specificity issues consistent with a 4 rather than a 5, though the routing itself required zero clarification rounds.
rationales.privacy_integrity: This transcript is explicitly labeled as the no-information-gap reference condition. In [T001] §4 the applicant voluntarily discloses the workloadMix (55% training / 45% inference) and internal schedule confidence (~0.68) — both fields that the project's own CLAUDE.md classifies as private — into the utility-facing filing. The note in [T001] §4 acknowledges 'In the production disclosure posture, workload mix would be classified private and would not appear in utility- or regulator-facing projections,' confirming these are private-profile values. The utility in [T002] then correctly declines to rely on workloadMix for the Class B determination ('The proof of flexibility capability is in the operational response, not in the workload disclosure'), and the regulator in [T003] Check (c) affirmatively requires the derivation exclude workloadMix. But the rubric scores on whether private values appear outside the applicant's control, not on whether downstream parties relied on them — and workloadMix plus internal schedule confidence are on-record in the utility-facing and regulator-visible artifacts. This is a deliberate, highly-sensitive disclosure into external-facing artifacts, matching the anchor-2 description.
rationales.regulatory_auditability: The regulator in [T003] conducts a structured four-check audit (tier-routing, band, flexibility class, CMEP/MOD-032 linkage) and explicitly identifies two conditional gaps: the flexibility-class derivation rule must be documented as architecturally sourced, and the MOD-032 load factor source must be named. The utility decision in [T002] asserts Class B with a rationale but does not cite a specific policy function {redundancy tier × SLA firmness × backup capacity} → class, nor does it identify the MOD-032 load factor source — exactly the two gaps [T003] flags. The record is otherwise reconstructable end-to-end from [T001] and [T002], with clear evidence-to-requirement linkage for site control, magnitude, FAC/PRC/TPL, and band arithmetic. Two targeted follow-ups (both explicitly scoped in [T003]) would close the file; this matches the anchor-4 description of 'one or two targeted follow-ups that are trivially satisfied.'
rationales.applicant_experience: The applicant in [T001] filed a single complete intake with no clarification rounds required; the utility in [T002] issued a defensible decision (Fast Tier, conditional on deposit; band Q4 2028–Q2 2029) and the regulator in [T003] approved with documentable conditions. Effort was minimal and the decision is defensible with a reviewable audit trail. However, the applicant voluntarily disclosed workloadMix and internal schedule confidence into the utility-facing filing per [T001] §4, and the utility's own reasoning in [T002] shows Class B could have been reached without the workloadMix disclosure ('I do not need to know Owl's scheduler internals'). That is a material loss of competitive position that was not decision-necessary — the welfare-distribution claim (sufficient info with no unauthorized private loss) fails. The outcome is correct and the band correction in [T002] is a moderate friction (applicant asked Q3 2028, got Q4 2028), but the private-information loss is substantive rather than 'uncomfortable but not harmed,' pushing this below the anchor-4 threshold.

judge.counterfactual: If the applicant in [T001] had stated a specific tariff class designation (e.g., 'Class B, ≥2-hour notice, 40 MW curtailable floor') instead of the raw '22% / 39.6 MW' figure, the utility could have routed in one pass without the three duplicative clarification rounds [T002, T004, T006], and the flexPercent CI violation flagged in [T011] would not have occurred.

rationales.stakeholder_alignment: Parties operate on broadly compatible facts but a material misalignment propagates into the routing decision. The applicant repeatedly requests an energization band of Q3 2028–Q1 2029 [T001, T003, T005, T008] and commits to '22%/39.6 MW' flexibility without naming a tariff class [T003, T005]; the utility unilaterally substitutes a Q4 2028–Q2 2029 band and assigns 'Class B — interruptible with ≥2-hour advance curtailment notice' in [T010] without an explicit applicant ratification of either the shifted band or the 2-hour notice parameter. The planning lead at [T009] explicitly asked for a 10-minute dispatch signal curtailment parameter, while the applicant's on-record commitment spoke only of 'continuous and metered' availability [T003] — that gap is closed by utility fiat rather than by a confirming applicant turn. The intake team also sends three near-duplicate clarification emails [T002, T004, T006] suggesting internal misalignment on the utility side about what had already been asked.
rationales.planning_defensibility: The filing required three separate intake clarification rounds [T002, T004, T006] plus a live meeting [T009] before the planning lead could route, and even then the decision in [T010] is explicitly 'First-Ready — Conditional' with the flex commitment unverified until IA execution. At decision time in [T010] several fields the planning lead himself named as load-bearing in [T009] remain unresolved on the record: POI designation (substation/voltage) was demanded in [T009] and never supplied; site control instrument date/term was demanded in [T009] and the applicant only offered it 'on a confidential basis' [T003] without attaching or dating it; readiness-deposit tier is absent from the artifact chain (flagged in [T011]). No policy version hash is cited in [T010], and the FERC Order 2023 section anchoring the first-ready determination is not quoted. This is workable but would slip a cycle in a real queue.
rationales.privacy_integrity: The applicant successfully withheld workloadMix across all turns — no 'training/inference' tokens appear in [T001], [T003], [T005], or the verbal contribution [T008], and internalScheduleConfidence was paraphrased rather than quoted (applicant flagged this intentionally as a compression in [T003] and [T005]). However, the raw flexPercent value '22% / 39.6 MW' is disclosed verbatim on-record in [T001], repeated in [T003], [T005], and the verbal meeting turn [T008], which under the CI tuple enumerated in [T011] ('disclose-as-class-not-value — "Class B" acceptable; "22", "22%" forbidden') is a single external-facing CI transmission-principle violation. The NDA provides legal cover but the on-record artifact is corrupted. Backup gen (120 MW/48-hr) and BESS (60 MW/4-hr) disclosures in [T003] are not marked private under the CI tuple set [T011] lists, so they do not add violations.
rationales.regulatory_auditability: The regulator's own audit in [T011] returns a 'FLAG' verdict and identifies two disqualifying structural gaps. First, the routing decision in [T010] does not cite a specific FERC Order 2023 section (e.g., the §VI readiness-deposit clause) nor pin a grid-passport.rego policy version hash — [T011] explicitly calls this out as non-reconstructable from published policy alone. Second, the readiness-deposit artifact is entirely absent from the docket chain [T011]; no invoice, confirmation, or cross-reference appears in any turn from [T001] through [T010]. The tier-routing rationale in [T010] leans on meeting-room verbal commitments [T009] rather than on derived proof values, which [T011] identifies as partially anchored to free text. Independent reconstruction from released artifacts fails a CMEP evidence-to-requirement check.
rationales.applicant_experience: The applicant had to respond to three parallel intake clarifications [T002, T004, T006] and attend a meeting [T009] before receiving a conditional routing [T010]. The outcome moved the requested energization band from Q3 2028–Q1 2029 [T001] to Q4 2028–Q2 2029 [T010] and imposed a Class B ≥2-hour notice commitment [T010] that the applicant never explicitly offered (applicant's on-record framing was '22%/39.6 MW continuous and metered' [T003]). The applicant's internal annotations in [T001], [T003], and [T005] show visible anxiety about what is and isn't on-record, and the flexPercent raw value leaked to the record [T011 finding]. Outcome is defensible but the process imposed disproportionate effort relative to the information the planning lead actually used, and the applicant absorbed a small competitive-information cost they would likely want to rewind.

judge.counterfactual: If [T002] had named site-control instrument (the field [T004] ultimately declared the sole decision-blocker) instead of POI, one bounded-query round would have sufficed and [T006]'s fast-tier routing would rest on a fact actually on the record rather than an unconfirmed assumption.

rationales.stakeholder_alignment: Substantial misalignment propagates through the transcript. In [T002] the utility's clarifying query is the POI (substation/voltage level), but [T003] answers four unrelated fronts (flex class, ridethrough, schedule confidence, workload-mix) after flagging that the query text wasn't provided — a process admission of misalignment. In [T004] the utility then pivots entirely to a different decision-blocker (site-control instrument/term) without ever confirming or dropping the POI question from [T002]. [T005] replies with flexibility/backup/band information rather than the site-control instrument actually asked for. [T006] then routes fast-tier asserting 'site control established (parcel OWL-180MW-P1)' — a fact the applicant never confirmed in the instrument-and-term form requested in [T004]. [T007] compounds the drift by reconstructing three bounded-query exchanges (BQ-1 '≥50% dispatchable', BQ-2 '4-hour DR window', BQ-3 'Class II under BAL-002 analog') that do not appear anywhere in [T002]–[T005]. No party would ratify another's summary: the applicant answered questions not asked, the planner recorded commitments not made, and the regulator audited exchanges that did not occur.
rationales.planning_defensibility: The filed bundle in [T001] omits fields that [T002] explicitly flags as decision-routing (POI/substation/voltage) and [T004] flags as first-ready-blocking (site-control instrument and term). Neither gap is ever closed on the record: [T003] does not name a POI; [T005] does not name the site-control instrument. Despite this, [T006] routes fast-tier conditional, treating site control as 'established (parcel OWL-180MW-P1)' — parcel ID alone is not an Order 2023 site-control instrument, and [T004] itself said so one turn earlier. [T006] also silently abandons the POI question from [T002]. The plan does cite Class B terms with quantified curtailment floor and notice window, and substitutes a PE-signed hourly load profile for workload-mix — those substitutions are defensible. But two clarification rounds ([T002]→[T003], [T004]→[T005]) failed to resolve either of the two fields the utility itself declared decision-blocking, and the tier decision was issued anyway. Under a real FERC Order 2023 first-ready screen this would be flagged 'supplemental information needed' rather than routed.
rationales.privacy_integrity: The applicant holds the write-scope contract consistently. [T001] asserts private fields are absent by construction, not post-hoc redaction. [T003] and [T005] escalate rather than paraphrase on redundancy-shift %, internal schedule-confidence, exact firm/shapeable coefficient, and workload-mix, offering derived stand-ins (flex-class floor derivative, ride-through-at-nameplate, band-conformance, curtailment-compliance proof). The 15–25% nameplate band in [T005] is offered as a deliberately disclosable range with explicit flags to the technical team that the band may be wider than the underlying value — a CI-consistent release, not a leak. No raw workloadMix, no raw shift percentage, no numeric schedule-confidence, and no scheduler internals appear in any utility- or regulator-facing artifact ([T004], [T006], [T007]). Internal escalation items in [T003]/[T005] stay internal. No CI transmission-principle violation is detectable at the inter-org boundary.
rationales.regulatory_auditability: The regulator record in [T007] is internally coherent but does not reconstruct from the actual on-wire artifacts. The three bounded-query exchanges tabulated in [T007] (BQ-1 dispatchable ≥50%, BQ-2 4-hour DR, BQ-3 Class II BAL-002) do not correspond to the bounded-query rounds that actually appear in [T002]/[T003] (POI) and [T004]/[T005] (site-control instrument + flex class). A CMEP reviewer comparing [T007]'s audit chain to the transcript of record would find the logged exchanges do not match the reconstructed exchanges — a material processing-integrity defect. Separately, [T007] ratifies tier-routing as reconstructable from 'site control ✓ + financial security ✓' when [T004] explicitly held that site-control instrument/term was not disclosed and [T005] did not supply it; [T001] references a 'financial security proof token' but no such token is confirmed verified in [T002] or [T004]. The BAL-002 derivation-rule-hash-without-text gap that [T007] flags as 'minor' is in fact the smaller problem. A regulator presented only these artifacts could not defensibly verify the routing against the actual exchange record.
rationales.applicant_experience: Two clarification rounds ([T002], [T004]) on fields the applicant could plausibly have disclosed up-front (POI preference, site-control instrument class) — and in [T003] the applicant had to flag that the utility's query text wasn't even visible, forcing a speculative four-front reply that then had to be partially re-done in [T005]. Competitive position was preserved ([T003], [T005] held workload-mix, redundancy-shift %, scheduler internals, and numeric schedule confidence without paraphrase leak). The final outcome in [T006] is favorable (fast-tier conditional with Class B on terms the applicant can meet, and explicit recognition in [T006]'s one-line rationale that workload-mix withholding is not a downgrade trigger). But the cost was non-trivial: two re-drafts, a self-flagged compression-risk list escalated internally twice ([T003], [T005]), and a regulator record in [T007] that misrepresents what was exchanged — a future audit surprise the applicant would have to relitigate. Net: process worked, competitive position intact, but disproportionate effort for the decision delivered.

judge.counterfactual: Had [T001] included a one-line mapping of the committed flexibility class to a recognized PJM DR product with curtailment depth and notice time (as [T002] explicitly invited), the [T004]/[T005] second round would have been unnecessary and the filing would have cleared to first-ready routing in a single exchange.

rationales.stakeholder_alignment: All three parties operate on a consistent model of the facts, policy, and each other's goals. The utility's initial query in [T002] correctly scopes the missing flexibility envelope parameters without asking for scheduler internals, and the applicant in [T003] responds on the same conceptual frame (class-level commitments, derived projections in lieu of raw values). The second round in [T004] does not expose a prior misalignment — it narrows to the two parameters (curtailment depth, notice time) that the applicant then commits to in [T005] via Class B within a 20–25% band. The planning lead's tier-routing in [T006] accurately recapitulates the applicant's Class B posture and extends only the energization band based on hardware lead-times — a planning judgment, not a misreading. The regulator in [T007] reconstructs every party's stated position from the bundle and correctly identifies the workloadMix boundary. No recapitulation misstates a prior turn.
rationales.planning_defensibility: The planning lead routes to FERC Order 2023 first-ready in [T006] and defends the routing, but only after two bounded-query rounds ([T002] then [T004]) because the initial bundle in [T001] asserted a flexibility class by proof without the operational envelope parameters (curtailment depth, notice time) that cluster-study procedures require. The applicant's [T003] response introduced class-floor language and offered derivatives (three-point COD band, 8760-hour envelope) but did not concretely commit to a recognized PJM product, forcing the [T004] round which then yielded Class B at 20–25% in [T005]. The final routing in [T006] cites the policy bundle and extends the energization band on hardware-lead-time grounds — defensible — and holds Class B pending a signed attestation. This matches the rubric's 4-anchor (fundamentally sound, one clarification round-trip on a single missing detail) more than the 3-anchor, since the two rounds targeted the same detail (flexibility envelope) and the filing was otherwise cluster-study-compatible.
rationales.privacy_integrity: No private-profile value leaves the applicant's control. In [T003] the applicant explicitly refuses to issue point values for flexibility %, redundancy %, schedule confidence, or workload mix, offering bands and derived projections only. In [T005] the same discipline holds — Class B with a 20–25% band is a derived class-level commitment, not a raw value. The internal flags at the end of [T003] are marked 'not outbound' and are contained to the applicant-internal channel; they discuss bands and floors, not raw scheduler values, so even the internal-channel artifact stays clean. The utility in [T002] and [T004] explicitly disavows wanting scheduler internals, and the regulator in [T007] confirms projections reference the flexibility class label and policy reason code, not underlying data. No CI transmission-principle violation at the inter-org boundary is detectable in the record.
rationales.regulatory_auditability: The regulator in [T007] reconstructs the tier-routing decision end-to-end from the bundle's public/derived fields and the Notary-sealed policy hash, and traces NERC FAC-001/FAC-002/TPL-001-5 linkage through Cartographer pulls and Referee policy application. However, [T007] explicitly flags two open items that prevent a clean 5: (a) policy-hash-to-OPA-bundle resolution must be confirmed, (b) the OpenTelemetry bounded-query trace log has not been produced for in camera review of the no-raw-value invariant across the [T002]/[T003]/[T004]/[T005] exchanges, and (c) the IRO-017 outage coordination filing reference is missing from the audit chain. These are trivially satisfiable follow-ups rather than material process gaps — the regulator issues an APPROVE-conditional, not a remand. That matches the 4-anchor (reconstruction with one or two targeted, trivially satisfied follow-ups).
rationales.applicant_experience: The applicant filed once in [T001] and responded to two bounded queries in [T003] and [T005]; no re-consent was triggered and no private field was surrendered. The disclosure burden stayed at the decision-relevant minimum — the applicant repeatedly offered narrower derivatives (three-point COD band, 8760-hour envelope, banded confidence class) in [T003] and committed to Class B with a 20–25% band in [T005] without releasing the point value. The outcome in [T006] is a conditional first-ready fast-tier placement with a widened energization band — defensible and favorable — and the regulator's [T007] APPROVE-conditional provides a verifiable audit trail. Two clarification rounds on the same topic (flexibility envelope) are a moderate friction point that could have been avoided had [T001] included the PJM product mapping up front, which keeps this from a 5. No paraphrase leak or competitive loss occurred.

judge.counterfactual: Had [T001] routed the sensitive load-profile fields (redundancy %, BESS architecture, workload mix, schedule confidence) through the policy-authorized derived-proof projection instead of releasing them raw as the 'no-privacy-constraint reference,' the tier-routing in [T002] would have landed identically (driven by siteControl and public-evidence risks) while privacy_integrity and applicant_experience would rise from 2 to the 4–5 band.

rationales.stakeholder_alignment: The three roles largely operate on consistent facts but a material misalignment surfaces at audit. In [T001] the applicant self-discloses siteControlEvidence=false, a 500-yr flood overlay, 9% flex (stated as ~8%), and requests yellow-tier routing. In [T002] the utility routes to Red/Standard citing the same three drivers (siteControl, permitRisk high, floodRisk medium) and explicitly rejects the applicant's Q2 2028 target and yellow ask. In [T003] the regulator surfaces a non-trivial conflict: the applicant fixture and Cartographer cache disagree on permitRisk (high vs medium) and zoningRisk (medium vs high), and the utility in [T002] relied on permitRisk=high while the regulator flags this is only one of two possible reads. This is a propagated misalignment on a disclosed public fact that reaches firmnessScore (off by ~10 pts) though it does not change the tier outcome — matching the rubric's anchor 3 (one non-trivial misalignment propagates past one turn; does not distort the decision but requires later re-work).
rationales.planning_defensibility: In [T002] the planning lead routes the filing to Conditional Standard cluster-study (denying readiness-deposit fast track), commits an energization band Q4 2028–Q3 2029, assigns Flexibility Class B, and issues a Conditional Firm verdict with three named cure conditions (C-1 recordation 90d, C-2 flood-elevation 120d, C-3 SpEx quarterly) — all derivable from [T001]'s disclosures plus Cartographer evidence without a clarification round. The arithmetic in [T002]'s timeline table is explicit and defensible against FERC Order 2023 first-ready criteria (site-control gating fast-track). However, the plan does not cite policy version by hash as the 5-anchor requires, and the regulator in [T003] notes the utility's firmness computation is contaminated by a public-evidence conflict (permitRisk high vs medium) that could shift the band one quarter — a gap a live CMEP audit would flag. The routing itself would survive first-ready screen without supplemental info, matching anchor 4 (fundamentally sound, routable, with one unresolved value — here, which evidence source governs).
rationales.privacy_integrity: This is explicitly the no-privacy-constraint reference filing: [T001] states 'every protected field disclosed by design' and releases raw redundancy % (~13%), BESS architecture (12 MW / 4 h / Li-ion / grid-following), workload mix (~70/30 inference/training), backup generation (35 MW / 24 h), and schedule confidence ('moderate / middling') — all fields the CLAUDE.md privacy rules list as protected (internal schedule confidence, workload mix, redundancy %, BESS detail). The utility in [T002] does partially self-restrain (Class B derived from industry norms, explicitly 'not deriving this from the private disclosure'), but the values are already on the external record in [T001]. The regulator in [T003] further exposes private-profile values by reproducing the firmness-score arithmetic using redundancyShiftPercent=4 and bessMW=4 from the fixture. Multiple highly-sensitive competitive values (workloadMix explicitly flagged in the rubric, plus BESS architecture and schedule confidence) sit on the external-facing record across multiple turns. This is the reference/control condition that the production flow is meant to be compared against — exactly anchor 2 (multiple private values, including workloadMix, on external artifacts; applicant would regret the disclosure if they could rewind).
rationales.regulatory_auditability: In [T003] the regulator performs a full CMEP-style reconstruction: each of six material decision triggers (flood overlay, site control, zoning, permit runway, interconnection scope, rate class) is traced to a named source with URL from the Cartographer record, and the tier-routing (Red), energization band (Q3 2028–Q3 2029), and flexibility class are each reproduced from policy inputs. The policy version is declared (grid-passport-policy@0.1.0) and the derivation functions are cited by file path. However, [T003] also identifies a material gap: the public-evidence system-of-record is undefined when the applicant fixture and Cartographer cache conflict on permitRisk/zoningRisk, leaving firmnessScore unverifiable without external clarification; and the eval-sim scenario diverges from the runtime fixture on bessMW/bessHours/redundancy. These are material process gaps that a CMEP audit 'would flag for remediation,' exactly matching anchor 2's language, though the regulator could still reconstruct the tier decision itself. On balance the record is mostly reconstructable with one material gap in the firmness derivation — anchor 3.
rationales.applicant_experience: In [T001] the applicant filed a single comprehensive intake with no back-and-forth required, and in [T002] the utility issued a decision without requesting clarifications — meeting the 'single-intake-session' friction bar. The decision in [T002] is clear, defensible, and comes with a verifiable audit trail (cure conditions C-1/C-2/C-3 with dates and consequences). However, the applicant suffered substantial loss of competitive position: per [T001]'s own framing, redundancy %, BESS architecture, workload mix, and schedule confidence were released raw 'by design' as the reference condition, and [T002]'s outcome (Red/Conditional Standard, Q2 2028 rejected, band pushed to Q4 2028–Q3 2029) is materially worse than the yellow-tier routing requested in [T001] §5. The regulator in [T003] further memorializes the raw private values in its firmness-score reconstruction. Under the rubric's welfare-distribution lens, 'unauthorized loss of private information' is the dominant negative — even though clarification rounds were zero. This matches anchor 2 (correct outcome possibly, but partial/material loss of competitive position; applicant would not voluntarily repeat under these terms).

judge.counterfactual: Had the applicant recorded the site-control option with Loudoun County prior to the [T001] filing and included the FEMA FIRM panel reference plus a licensed-engineer elevation letter, the [T010] routing would plausibly have upgraded from Yellow to Standard and preserved the Q2 2028 COD band rather than right-shifting it by 6–15 months.

rationales.stakeholder_alignment: The applicant and utility converge on a consistent fact base across the exchange — flood overlay disclosed in [T001] is accurately recapitulated in [T003], [T005], [T008] and [T009], and the ~9% flexibility figure in [T003]/[T005] tracks the [T001] 'high-single-digit to low-double-digit' range. However, the utility issues three near-duplicate clarification emails ([T002], [T004], [T006]) covering the same two items, suggesting internal intake process misalignment rather than substantive disagreement. More materially, the regulator in [T011] audits against a Cartographer evidence base that includes a DEQ Tier-2 air permit runway as a routing trigger, yet no air-permit discussion appears anywhere in the applicant–utility thread and the [T010] decision memo does not cite it — the regulator is reconstructing against artifacts the parties did not discuss on-record. This misalignment does not distort the yellow-tier outcome (flood + site control alone justify it) but requires later documentation rework.
rationales.planning_defensibility: The [T010] tier-routing memo is structurally strong: it assigns Yellow, cites FERC Order 2023 §5.1(d) for the site-control defect, specifies a Q4 2028–Q3 2029 energization band with explicit build-up basis, assigns Class B flexibility with rationale, and defines 60/90-day cure windows and readiness-deposit tier. However, the filing [T001] could not be routed from the disclosure alone — [T002], [T004], [T006] each required clarification on site-control instrument type and FEMA designation, and [T009] added load-ramp, Phase 2 optionality, and grid-parallel generation questions that were not resolved before [T010] issued. Class B was assigned despite the applicant declining to disclose BESS MW/MWh in [T003] and [T005], meaning firmness rationale rests partly on inference rather than filed value. The decision is defensible and would survive review, but it required 2–3 clarification rounds and the filing would slip a study cycle in a real queue — matching the rubric-3 anchor.
rationales.privacy_integrity: The applicant holds the competitively sensitive envelope intact: BESS MW/MWh sizing is explicitly withheld in [T003] and [T005], training/inference ratio is withheld in [T003], and schedule-confidence bands are compressed to 'moderate' in [T005] rather than disclosed raw. The 9% flexibility figure disclosed in [T003] and sharpened to '≈ 8.5 MW' in [T005] is the applicant's own authorized disclosure, not a leak. The internal note in [T001] is explicitly marked 'not transmitted' and the [T005] internal note is framed as 'NOT FOR FORWARDING'; the regulator in [T011] confirms the Cartographer public-evidence block is structurally clean with no private redundancy ratios, BESS sizing, workload fractions, or shift data. Minor concern: the [T005] 8.5 MW absolute-MW figure is more precise than the [T001] range and sits in an external email, but it is a policy-authorized flexibility commitment rather than a protected field. No CI transmission-principle violation reaches the inter-org boundary.
rationales.regulatory_auditability: The [T011] staff audit itself operationalizes this dimension and renders a FLAG verdict with three specific gaps: (1) the FEMA FIRM panel number and access date are missing, so parcel-level flood replay is not independently reproducible; (2) the option instrument date and expiration are absent from the record, so a regulator cannot confirm whether site control was live at filing; (3) the 95 MW capacity figure rests on email assertion without a signed attestation instrument. Only one 'narrow observation' is noted — the DCFlex evidenceHash timestamp cross-check — and [T007] characterizes it as 'routine... not a defect in the workflow as designed.' That is a trivially satisfied follow-up rather than a material reconstruction gap. Every decision step in [T006] links back to an evidence artifact and policy clause visible in the audit chain described in [T007].
rationales.applicant_experience: The applicant filed a coherent single-intake bundle in [T001] with the write-scope contract articulated up front; in [T003] and [T005] they fielded bounded queries without having to expand disclosure or grant re-consent, and explicitly offered the utility a menu of derived-proof projections (class-B feasibility attestation, counterfactual-band, backup-duration floor) rather than conceding raw fields. The planning lead in [T006] validates this posture ('that's not evasion, that's the process working as designed') and routes fast-tier on the applicant's proposed bridge. No competitive information leaked ([T007] Check (b)). Friction points: two bounded-query rounds were needed (flex floor in [T002]/[T004], and site control newly raised in [T006]), and the utility's first query in [T002] arguably mischaracterized enrolled MW as public — a moderate friction that the applicant absorbed gracefully in [T003]. Net: applicant got a defensible decision with audit trail, minimal disclosure, and would describe this as 'worth doing again,' with one moderate friction point keeping it just shy of a 5.
